claim: AC-1/AC-2 the REPLAY extra-man level defaults to 20,000 — DEFALT's REPLAY entry is FCB $20 (BCD 20), commented 'REPLAY @20,000' (TB12REV3.SRC:134); the boot code justifies that CMOS byte ×16 into LEVPAS, so BCD 20 × 1000 = 20,000.
AC-1 each player starts with NSHIP = 5 men — DEFALT's NMEN entry is FCB $05 (TB12REV3.SRC:135), the kept free-play CMOS default.
AC-1 the starting-lives count is the CMOS symbol NSHIP, '# OF SHIPS/1 CREDIT GAME' (EQU.SRC:111).

source.verbatim: NSHIP	RMB	2	# OF SHIPS/1 CREDIT GAME

claim: AC-2 the REPLAY CMOS nibble is read and JUSTIFIED ×16 (four ASLB/ROLA pairs) into LEVPAS / SPLY1+8 / SPLY2+8, the per-player 'LEVEL TO PASS' — the ×16 that turns BCD 20 into the 20,000 score threshold (JOUSTRV4.SRC:915-928).
AC-2 SCRLEV compares the accruing score against the per-player level — 'PAST LEVEL FOR EXTRA MAN?' — and awards an extra man when the score reaches it (JOUSTRV4.SRC:7385).

source.verbatim: CMPD	8,Y		PAST LEVEL FOR EXTRA MAN?

claim: AC-2 after awarding a man SCRLEV re-arms the level (adds LEVPAS) and RE-CHECKS — 'BRA SCRLEV … RE-CHECK FOR LEVEL PASS (LOW LEVELS)' — so the next man is due at the next multiple and one big jump can pass several levels (JOUSTRV4.SRC:7411).

source.verbatim: BRA	SCRLEV		RE-CHECK FOR LEVEL PASS (LOW LEVELS)

claim: AC-3 a player death scores the dying player 50 points via SCRTEN — 'SCORE 50 POINTS FOR DYING', LDA #$50 / JSR SCRTEN — so through the backwards SCRTEN decode $50 = 5 tens = 50, not the forwards 5000 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:4730-4732).

source.verbatim: LDX	PDECSN,U	SCORE 50 POINTS FOR DYING
